All 9 tests pass now (`node --test`: 9 pass, 0 fail). I changed one line in each of the two source files and didn't touch the tests.

**Bug 1: `src/bill.js` gave out one cent too many (off-by-one).**
`splitBill` adds an extra cent to each of the first `leftover` people, but the check was `i <= leftover`, so one more person than intended got a cent. Even an even split went wrong: `splitBill(900, 3)` has `leftover = 0`, but person 0 still got a cent, giving `[301, 300, 300]`, and the total no longer matched the bill. This one bug caused all three bill test failures. Fix: `i < leftover`.

**Bug 2: `src/duration.js` accepted input with junk around a valid duration.**
`parseDuration` collected every `\d+[hms]` match it found anywhere in the string and only failed if there were none. So `"10m and change"` returned 600 instead of throwing. Fix: the whole string must now match `^(\d+[hms])+$` before it is parsed, otherwise it throws `SyntaxError`. The existing parsing code is unchanged.

One thing I left alone: the parser still accepts a repeated unit like `"1h1h"` and adds the values up. No test covers that case, and keeping the change minimal meant not deciding it here.

I did this myself without delegating because the fix was small.
